## Today's questions {#roadmap data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

- Which plot matches the question and the variables?
- How do we build and annotate it in base R?
- How does ggplot2 express the same choices?

**Case study** · What changes in a vitamin C dose-response plot when we show the delivery method?

## R graphics packages {#packages data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

| Tool | Typical use |
|:---|:---|
| Base R graphics | Quick plots and direct control over drawing |
| ggplot2 | Layered figures with consistent scales and panels |
| lattice | Trellis plots for comparisons across groups |
| plotly | Interactive figures with hover, zoom and pan |

Base graphics ships with R. Today we use base graphics first, then ggplot2.

## Plot choice by question {#plot-choices data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

| Question | Variables | Plot |
|:---|:---|:---|
| How variable is length? | One numeric variable | Histogram |
| How many animals got each dose? | Categories and counts | Bar chart |
| Does length vary with dose? | Two numeric variables | Scatterplot |
| Does length differ by delivery method? | Numeric outcome and groups | Boxplot |
| How does concentration change over time? | Ordered measurements | Line plot |
| How do group summaries vary across two factors? | Two groups and a summary | Heatmap |

## Starting and adding to a base plot {#base-high-low data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

| High-level calls start a plot | Low-level calls add to it |
|:---|:---|
| `plot()`, `hist()`, `boxplot()`, `barplot()` | `points()`, `lines()`, `abline()` |
| Set up axes and plotting coordinates | `text()`, `legend()`, `axis()`, `title()` |

Run the high-level call first. A later high-level call starts the next plot or panel.

## Base R histogram {#base-histogram .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Each bar counts measurements in an interval. Bin width changes what patterns you can see.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
growth <- ToothGrowth
hist(growth$len, breaks = seq(0, 35, by = 5),
     xlab = "Odontoblast length", main = "",
     col = "#56B4E9", border = "white")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/base-histogram-1.png){fig-alt='Histogram of odontoblast length in five-unit intervals.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Base R bar chart {#base-bars .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Treat each tested dose as a category. The bars show how many animals received it.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
barplot(table(growth$dose),
        xlab = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
        ylab = "Animals", col = "#56B4E9")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/base-bars-1.png){fig-alt='Bar chart showing 20 animals at each of the three doses.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Base R scatterplot {#base-scatter .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Each point is one animal. There are only three x positions, and some points overlap.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(len ~ dose, data = growth,
     xlab = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
     ylab = "Odontoblast length",
     pch = 16, col = "#0072B2")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/base-scatter-1.png){fig-alt='Odontoblast lengths plotted at the three vitamin C doses.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Adding points and a legend {#base-overlay .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Start an empty plot with `type = "n"`. Draw one group at a time, then explain the symbols.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(len ~ dose, data = growth, type = "n",
     xlab = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
     ylab = "Odontoblast length")
with(subset(growth, supp == "OJ"),
     points(dose, len, pch = 16, col = "#0072B2"))
with(subset(growth, supp == "VC"),
     points(dose, len, pch = 17, col = "#D55E00"))
legend("bottomright",
       c("Orange juice", "Ascorbic acid"),
       pch = c(16, 17),
       col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"),
       bty = "n")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/base-overlay-1.png){fig-alt='Dose response scatterplot distinguishing orange juice and ascorbic acid by color and shape.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Base R boxplot {#base-boxplot .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

The middle line is the median. The box shows the middle half. Each box is one dose and delivery method.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
boxplot(len ~ supp + dose, data = growth,
        xlab = "Method and dose (mg/day)",
        ylab = "Odontoblast length",
        col = c("#A6D7ED", "#F4BA9B"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/base-boxplot-1.png){fig-alt='Six boxplots for orange juice and ascorbic acid at each dose.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Base R line plot {#base-line .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Indomethacin concentration over time for one person. Each point is one blood sample.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
one <- subset(Indometh, Subject == "1")
one <- one[order(one$time), ]
plot(conc ~ time, data = one, type = "b",
     xlab = "Time since dose (hours)",
     ylab = "Plasma concentration (mcg/mL)",
     pch = 16, lwd = 2, col = "#0072B2")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/base-line-1.png){fig-alt='Indomethacin plasma concentration over time for one subject.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Base R graphics settings {#base-par data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

`par("mar")` reads a setting. `par(mfrow = c(1, 2))` changes the active device's layout for subsequent plots.

| Setting | Controls |
|:---|:---|
| `mfrow`, `mar` | Panel rows and columns, margins (bottom, left, top, right) |
| `pch`, `col`, `cex` | Point symbol, colour, relative size |
| `lty`, `lwd` | Line type and width |
| `las`, `cex.axis`, `cex.lab` | Axis tick-label orientation, tick text and axis title size |

Set labels and limits on a plot with `xlab`, `ylab`, `xlim` and `ylim`.

## Base R panels with a common scale {#base-panels .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Save the settings, draw both panels with the same y limits, then restore the settings.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
old <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1), las = 1)
for (method in c("OJ", "VC")) {
  group <- subset(growth, supp == method)
  boxplot(len ~ dose, data = group,
          main = method, ylim = range(growth$len),
          xlab = "Dose (mg/day)", ylab = "Length")
}
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/base-panels-1.png){fig-alt='Side-by-side boxplots by dose for each delivery method, with identical vertical scales.' width=576}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
par(old)
```
:::


## Reading the dose response {#base-check data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

- Which plot best shows whether the delivery methods differ at each dose?
- At which dose do the two groups look most alike?
- What can a histogram hide when we pool all the animals?

The base graphics section ends here.

## ggplot2 {#ggplot2-intro data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

A plotting package built around the **layered grammar of graphics**.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages("ggplot2")  # Once per R installation
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)
```
:::


[ggplot2 function reference](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/)

## What “grammar of graphics” means {#grammar data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

A chart is assembled from parts that can be reused and combined. Describe how the data should appear, one choice at a time.

| Part | Our dose-response scatterplot |
|:---|:---|
| Data | One row per animal |
| Mapping (`aes()`) | Dose goes on x, length on y, method controls colour |
| Geometry (`geom_point()`) | Draw each animal as a point |
| Scale and coordinates | Translate values to colours and positions on x and y |
| Facets and theme | Split into panels if useful, then style the display |

A **stat** may summarize rows before drawing them. A histogram counts rows within bins.

## The same scatterplot in ggplot2 {#gg-scatter .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Read it from top to bottom. Choose the data, map columns, then add a layer of points.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p <- ggplot(growth, aes(x = dose, y = len)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = supp, shape = supp),
             size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
       y = "Odontoblast length",
       colour = "Method", shape = "Method")
p
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/gg-scatter-1.png){fig-alt='ggplot2 dose response scatterplot with delivery method mapped to color and shape.' width=576}
:::
:::


## One row, one observation {#gg-data data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

| Dataset | What one row represents | What connects the rows |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `ToothGrowth` | One animal | Animals share a dose and delivery method |
| `Indometh` | One blood sample | Several samples come from the same person |

To draw one concentration curve per person in ggplot2, map `group = Subject` in the line layer.

## Aesthetics and constants {#gg-aes data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

**Map a column** inside `aes()`. `aes(colour = supp)` assigns colours by method and creates a guide.

**Set a constant** outside `aes()`. `colour = "steelblue"` gives every point the same colour.

Other aesthetics include `x`, `y`, `shape`, `fill`, `size`, `alpha` and `linetype`. Use `group` to tell a line layer which points belong together.

## Geometries and summaries {#gg-geoms data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

| Layer | Marks or summary |
|:---|:---|
| `geom_point()` | Individual observations |
| `geom_line()` | Connected measurements, ordered by x within group |
| `geom_bar()` / `geom_col()` | Count rows / draw supplied heights |
| `geom_histogram()` | Count rows within numeric intervals |
| `geom_boxplot()` | Show a distribution within each group |
| `geom_tile()` | Draw a tile at each x and y combination |

## Histogram bins in ggplot2 {#gg-hist .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

The histogram layer counts observations. Match the bin boundaries before comparing to the base plot.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(growth, aes(x = len)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0,
                 fill = "#56B4E9",
                 colour = "white") +
  labs(x = "Odontoblast length", y = "Animals")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/gg-hist-1.png){fig-alt='Histogram of odontoblast length with five-unit bins in ggplot2.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Grouped boxplots in ggplot2 {#gg-box .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Make dose a factor to give the three tested doses their own categories. Map delivery method to the fill.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(growth, aes(x = factor(dose), y = len,
                   fill = supp)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
       y = "Odontoblast length", fill = "Method")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/gg-box-1.png){fig-alt='Grouped boxplots by dose and delivery method.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Facets share a scale {#gg-facets .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Show one delivery method per panel. The default shared y scale makes the panels comparable.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(growth, aes(x = factor(dose), y = len)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#A6D7ED") +
  facet_wrap(~ supp) +
  labs(x = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
       y = "Odontoblast length")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/gg-facets-1.png){fig-alt='Separate panels for orange juice and ascorbic acid boxplots on a common scale.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Heatmap of group means {#gg-heat .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Reduce to one row per tile first. A tile shows the mean for a group and hides variation within it.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
means <- aggregate(len ~ supp + dose, growth, mean)
ggplot(means, aes(x = supp, y = factor(dose),
                  fill = len)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(len, 1)),
            colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#315E85",
                      high = "#113045") +
  labs(x = "Delivery method", y = "Dose (mg/day)",
       fill = "Mean length")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/gg-heat-1.png){fig-alt='Heatmap showing the mean odontoblast length for the six dose and method groups.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Scales, axes and guides {#gg-scales .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

A mapping says which variable controls colour. The scale chooses the colours and sets the legend labels.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
method_labels <- c("Orange juice", "Ascorbic acid")
p_scaled <- p +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(OJ = "#0072B2", VC = "#D55E00"),
    labels = method_labels
  ) +
  scale_shape_discrete(labels = method_labels)
p_scaled
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/gg-scales-1.png){fig-alt='Scatterplot with ticks at the tested doses and a legend spelling out the delivery methods.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Themes and labels {#gg-themes .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

A theme controls the look of the display. `labs()` supplies its wording.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p_final <- p_scaled +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Vitamin C and odontoblast length")
p_final
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/gg-themes-1.png){fig-alt='Dose-response scatterplot with a classic theme, descriptive title and bottom legend.' width=576}
:::
:::


## Saving a figure {#gg-save data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggsave("dose-response.png", plot = p_final,
       width = 7, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```
:::


Pass the plot object explicitly. The filename extension chooses the file format. Use PDF or SVG when you need scalable graphics.

## Choosing a plot for a new question {#wrap-up data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

A colleague has a numeric outcome for patients in three groups and wants to see spread, typical values and unusual observations.

1. Which plot would you start with?
2. What does one row represent?
3. What would you map to x and y, and what would your caption say?

## Extension · Data in two time series {#deaths-source data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

The two UK lung disease series share a calendar. The object name identifies the sex group.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
head(cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths), 3)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
         mdeaths fdeaths
Jan 1974    2134     901
Feb 1974    1863     689
Mar 1974    1877     827
```


:::
:::


To compare when counts peak, keep the calendar month and make sex a column.

## Extension · One variable per column {#deaths-tidy .plot-example data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

Stack the counts and attach each series to the same sequence of calendar months.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
months <- seq(as.Date("1974-01-01"), by = "month",
              length.out = length(mdeaths))
deaths <- data.frame(
  month = rep(months, times = 2),
  sex = rep(c("Male", "Female"),
            each = length(months)),
  count = c(as.numeric(mdeaths),
            as.numeric(fdeaths))
)
ggplot(deaths, aes(month, count, colour = sex)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Deaths", colour = "Sex")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-revealjs/deaths-tidy-1.png){fig-alt='Monthly death counts by sex in the UK from 1974 to 1979.' width=576}
:::
:::


## References and extensions {#gg-extension data-background="./_extensions/emc/www/triangle1.svg"}

- [R help for ToothGrowth](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/ToothGrowth.html) and [Indometh](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/Indometh.html)
- [R help for UK lung disease deaths](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/UKLungDeaths.html)
- [R help for graphical parameters](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/graphics/html/par.html)
- [The layered grammar of graphics](https://ggplot2-book.org/mastery.html) and the [ggplot2 reference](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/)
- [ggplot2 extension gallery](https://exts.ggplot2.tidyverse.org/gallery/)

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
